newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Got the Hong Kong handover blues? Surf the Net!.
newsitem.headline: Got the Hong Kong handover blues? Surf the Net!.

text.p: By Kurt Schork http://www.hk97.com
Hong Kong's impending handover to China got you down? Tired of that nostalgia for empire? Bored by Britain and Beijing?
Get with it. Get wired. Let the Internet whet your appetite for what's happening in Hong Kong leading up to, on and after June 30.

Scores of World Wide Web sites are serving up a smorgasbord of juicy Hong Kong factoids. Given that Hong Kong is the subject, it should come as no surprise there's a wealth of knowledge to be had from the net.
After all, this is a hi-tech city where kids tote miniature computerised pets known as "tamagotchi" around on key chains and parents take their mobile phones for a walk.

But let the surfer beware! A review of 97 Hong Kong-related sites listed in June's issue of The Dataphile magazine reveals many which are literate and useful and others ranging from useless to tasteless to weird and offbeat. Boring they're not.

The South China Morning Post http://www.scmp.com/1997 offers comprehensive coverage of events surrounding Hong Kong's transfer from Britain to China after a colonial interlude of more than 150 years. Ideal for the general interest surfer.

Those who worry about not being able to tell the difference between a T-69 tank and a T-54 when the People's Liberation Army rolls across the border from China into Hong Kong can check out http://www.cs.umanitoba.ca/jdeng/english/chinamil/tank/ index.htm. Colour photographs of Chinese armour will help.
Should you hanker for a handover meal of cooked dog and be unable to make it to Hong Kong for the real thing, take heart.
There's at least one web site that provides a recipe. You can find it if you try. No help from this vegetarian. Bring your own soy sauce. Lots of it.
And if you're uncertain which beverage should accompany that curried canine there's a delightful stop for tea connoisseurs at http://www.best.com:80/smurman/tea/.
Contributors to the lore on this site will not be mistaken for oenologists, as one review of 'petrified wood' tea makes clear.

"I carefully poured the tea into my mug and then brought the mug to my face and noticed the distinct smell of Yellowstone National Park in the (United) States," the reviewer writes. Make mine Liptons, thanks.
There's also a web site promoting "Unity - The Great Hong Kong Handover Party" as an an "awesome display of globally hip talent".
If you're more interested in shutting out the noise from the handover celebrations than listening, check out http://www.eartronix. com/ for the "latest in ear plug and noise suppressor technology".

The beat goes on for those taking the party line on the handover. There's a site with digitally recorded songs in praise of Mao Zedong and the Chinese Communist Party and another offering speeches from the Great Helmsman himself.
Or you can cut straight to the chase at http://www.staff.uiuc.edu/ f-zhang/mao.html for a full list of Mao sites.

If you like your handover pap with a ribald snap the site at http://humor.ncy.com:80/type/limerick/ has several offerings which rely far more on the rhyming potential of China and Hong Kong than any discernible poetic ablility. Parental guidance advised.
There's a Hong Kong Tourist Association site which can help with hotels.
With well over 300,000 references to Hong Kong on the Web you can find out just about anything you want to know and have fun doing it. The Reuters handover site is at http://www.hk97.com.
